name: Germinoma of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of germinoma with large cells, clear cytoplasm, and lymphocytic infiltration
MRI showing a well-demarcated, homogeneously enhancing mass in typical midline locations (pineal or suprasellar regions)
Normal or mildly elevated beta-hCG and normal alpha-fetoprotein in serum and CSF

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Tumor markers help differentiate germinoma from non-germinomatous germ cell tumors

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly associated with pineal region tumors
searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diabetes insipidus due to hypothalamic involvement

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
hormone deficiency causing slow growth and amenorrhea
walking problems from brain fluid buildup

occasional.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies other than vertical gaze palsy
searchTerms: weakness of facial or eye muscles
cranial nerve weakness except vertical gaze

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated beta-hCG in serum and CSF
CSF cytology usually negative for malignant cells
imaging: MRI showing homogeneously enhancing mass in pineal or suprasellar region
Hydrocephalus due to obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid pathways
Absence of hemorrhage or necrosis typical for germinoma
other: Histopathology demonstrating large cells with clear cytoplasm and lymphocytic infiltrate
Immunohistochemistry positive for placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) and c-KIT (CD117)

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein or beta-hCG less common
Elevated serum and CSF alpha-fetoprotein and beta-hCG
Histopathology showing embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, or choriocarcinoma components
Poorer prognosis and different treatment protocols

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
Endocrine dysfunction such as diabetes insipidus or hypopituitarism
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Matsutani M, et al. Intracranial germ cell tumors: diagnosis and treatment. J Neurooncol. 2001.
